rationale: Identity is `(kind, resolved name)`, so a selector written N times is ONE symbol and the repetitions are provenance, not nodes. Before the fix identity was the node's own RANGE, so every rule re-published its selector: 36.6% of corpus files carried an ambiguous name, the same selector up to 12 times, and a `contains` edge addressed one of N indistinguishable rows — so "what is inside this rule" had no single answer. The pins are per-NAME rather than a total, because a total would also pass if the lane published `.btn` once and `.btn:hover` zero times. `.btn:hover` and `.btn::before` are separate symbols: a pseudo-class is part of the selector's identity, not a variant of the base rule's identity.
